prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-02-18. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 0.94 |
| Retained earnings       | 21,891M |
| Current liabilities     | 9,428M |
| Current assets          | 8,827M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 36,034M |
| Total liabilities       | 50,185M |
| Total assets            | 86,783M |
| EBIT / operating income | 467M |
| Revenue                 | 5,013M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-02-18, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The reported current ratio below 1 signals weak liquidity and negative working capital. High leverage (total liabilities ~58% of assets) combined with very thin EBIT margins (~9%) and low asset turnover point to elevated default risk, placing the credit firmly in the speculative-grade range but not yet near-term distress.
DECISION: BB-
(The data are also consistent with a capital-intensive regulated utility or infrastructure entity whose stable cash flows could support a higher rating, but that cannot be assumed from the given figures alone.)
